an instruction, charge, command: , , , . (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)†

G3865.as:
* παρα-θεωρέω, -ῶ,
1. to examine side by side, compare.
2. to overlook, neglect: pass., .†

G3832.as:
πανοικεί (Rec., LTr., -κί), adv. (< πᾶς, οἶκος), a word rejected by strict Atticists, though found once in Plat. (Eryx., 392 c); [in LXX: Ex 1:1 (בַּיִת), III Mac 3:27 (where A in each case reads -κίᾳ, the Attic form, cf. Ge 50:8, al.)*;]
with all the household: .†

G3846.as:
παρα-βάλλω, [in LXX: Pr 2:2 4:20 5:1, 13 22:17 (נטה hi.), Ru 2:16 (שׁלל), II Mac 14:38 (elsewhere as v.l.4)*;]
1. to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.).
2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): , Rec.
3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, .
4. In mid. = παρα-βολεύομαι, q.v.†

G3896.as:
* παρα-πλέω,
to sail by or past: c. acc., .†

G3891.as:
παρα-νομέω, ῶ, [in LXX for חלל, etc., chiefly in Pss and II Mac;]
to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: .†

G3839.as:
** πάντῃ (Rec. -τη), adv. (< πᾶς), [in LXX: Si 50:22, III Mac 4:1*;]
every way, entirely: .†

G3805.as:
* παθητός, -ή, -όν (< πάσχω),
1. one who has suffered.
2. subject to suffering (R, mg., v. M, Pr., 222) or destined to suffer (AV, R, txt.): .†

G3881.as:
* παρα-λέγω,
to lay beside; mid.,
(a) to lie beside (Hom.);
(b) later, of sailors, to sail past: c. acc., , .†

G3867.as:
** παρ-αινέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Mac 7:25, 26, III Mac 5:17 7:12*;]
to exhort, advise: c. acc. pers. et inf. (v. Bl., § 72, 5; M, Pr., 205), ; absol., seq. λέγων, .†

G3806.as:
πάθος, -ους, τό (< πάσχω), [in LXX: Jb 30:31 (אֵבֶל), Pr 25:20, and very freq. in IV Mac (1:1 ff., al.)*;] like πάθημα;
1. that which befalls one, that which one suffers.
2. a passive emotion or affection (esp. of violent emotion), a passion, passionate desire; in NT always in bad sense: ; π. ἀτιμίας, ; π. ἐπιθυμίας, .†
SYN.: π. = πάθημα, exc. that πάθημα is the more concrete and particular. In NT usage, π. represents the passive, ungoverned aspect of evil desire, as opp. to ἐπιθυμία, which is the active and also the more comprehensive term (v. Tr., Syn., lxxxvii); cf. also ὄρεξις.

G3810.as:
παιδευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (< παιδεύω), [in LXX: Ho 5:2 (מוּסָר), Si 37:19, IV Mac 5:34 9:6*;]
1. prop., a teacher, instructor: .
2. a corrector, one who disciplines (cf. Ho 5:2): .†

G3847.as:
παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ (< παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Ps 100 (101):3 (סֵטִים), IV Ki 2:24 A, Wi 14:31, II Mac 15:10*;]
1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.).
2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaph., transgression (Plut., al.): , ; τ. νόμου, ; ἐν π., ; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, .
SYN.: v.s. ἁμαρτία.

G3848.as:
** παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ (< παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Ps 16 (17):4 138 (139):19, Je 6:28*;]
1. one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (cf. παραβαίνω, 1).
2. a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): , ; π. νόμου, , , .†

G3876.as:
* παρ-ακοή, -ῆς, ἡ,
1. a hearing amiss (Plat.).
2. Later, as following inattention, disobedience: , , (cf. παρακούω, and v. Tr., Syn., § lxvi).†

G3804.as:
* πάθημα, -τος, τό (< πάσχω), like πάθος,
1. that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., , , , , , , ; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., ; τ. Χριστσῦ, ; id. as shared by Christians, , , .
2. a passive emotion, affection, passion: ; τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, .
3. = τὸ πάσχειν, an enduring or suffering: c. gen. obj., .†
SYN.: v.s. πάθος.

G3821.as:
* παλαιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< παλαιός),
oldness: γράμματος, .†

G3873.as:
** παρά-κειμαι, [in LXX: Jdt.3.2, 3, Si 30:18 34 (31):16, Da LXX Bel 1:14, II, III Mac5*;]
to lie beside, be near, be present: , .†

G3863.as:
† παρα-ζηλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: De 32:21, III Ki 14:22, Ps 77 (78):58 (קנא pi., hi.), Ps 36 (37):1, 7, 8 (חרה hith.), Si 30:3*;]
to provoke to jealousy: (LXX) , , .†

G3807.as:
* παιδαγωγός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παῖς, ἄγω),
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opp. to πατήρ, ; fig., of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, , .†

G3815.as:
παίζω (< παῖς), [in LXX: Ge 21:9 26:8, Ex 32:6 (צחק pi.); and more freq. (Jg 16:25, al.) for (שׁחק pi.;]
prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing): (LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).†

G3889.as:
** παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ (< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 19:12*;]
1. encouragement, exhortation.
2. comfort, consolation: .†
SYN.: παράκλησις.

G3887.as:
παρα-μένω, [in LXX: Pr 12:7, Da TH 11:17 (עמד), etc.;]
to remain beside or near: , ; of remaining alive, (WH, κατα-), (cf. συμ-παραμένω).†

G3841.as:
† παντοκράτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (< πᾶς, κρατέω), [in LXX: freq. in Jb 5:8, 17, al. (שַׁדַּי), and for צְבָאוֹת, in the phrase θεός (κυρίος) π., II Ki 5:10, al., and freq. in Am, Za, Ma; also in Wi 7:25, Si 42:17 50:14, 17, and freq. in Jth, II, III Mac;]
almighty: , , , .†

G3835.as:
πανοῦργος, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for עָרוּם;]
ready to do anything;
(a) in cl., chiefly in bad sense, knavish, crafty: ;
(b) in good sense, skilful, clever (Pr 13:1 28:2).†

G3809.as:
παιδεία (-ία, T), -ας, ἡ (< παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּסָר;]
1. the rearing of a child (Æsch.).
2. training, learning, instruction (Plat., al.): , .
3. As in LXX (Pr 3:11 15:5, al.), chastening, discipline: (LXX), , , .†

G3823.as:
* πάλη, -ης, ἡ (< πάλλω, to sway)
wrestling, hence, generally, fight, contest: fig., of the spiritual combat of Christians, .†

G3890.as:
** παραμύθιον, -ου, τό (< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Wi 3:18*;]
1. an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; v. Lft. and ICC, ).
2. assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wi 3:18, and freq. in cl.).†

G3897.as:
* παρα-πλήσιος, -α, -ον (Hdt., Plat., al.; also -ος, -ον, Thuc., Polyb.),
coming near, nearly resembling. Neut. -ον, adverbially, = ίως, in a way nearly resembling: c. dat., .†

G3851.as:
*† παρα-βολεύομαι
= cl. παραβάλλομαι (II Mac 14:38),
to expose oneself to danger, hazard one's life: c. dat. ref., τ. ψυχῇ (v. M, Pr., 64), (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.†

G3884.as:
παρα-λογίζομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רמה pi.;]
1. to miscalculate.
2. to reason falsely, hence, to mislead: , .†

G3859.as:
*† παρα-δια-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ,
useless wrangling: v.l. in Rec. for διαπαρατριβή (q.v.), .†

G3866.as:
παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (< παρατίθημι), [in LXX: Le 6:2, 4 (5:21, 23) (פִּקָּדוֹן), and in To 10:13, II Mac 3:10, 15, v.l. for παρακαταθήκη (q.v.)*;]
a deposit or trust: , , (for exx. of this form, v. MM, Exp., iii, xviii).†

G3898.as:
** παρα-πλησίως, adv. (< παραπλήσιος), [in Quint.: Ho 8:6*;]
in like manner: .†

G3894.as:
† παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παραπικραίνω), [in LXX: Ps 94 (95):8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Ex 17:7; ἀντιλογία, De 33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Nu 20:24)*;]
provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), , (LXX).†

G3893.as:
† παρα-πικραίνω, [in LXX chiefly for מרה qal., hi., מְרִי, most freq. in Pss and Ez;]
to embitter, provoke: absol. (yet sc. τ. θεόν, cf. Ps 105 (106):7, Ez 2:5-8, al., and with τὸν θ. added, Ps 5:4, Ez 20:21, al.), (cf. παραπικρασμός).†

G3895.as:
παρα-πίπτω, [in LXX: Ez 14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 (מעל), 22:4 (אשׁם), Es 6:10 (נפל hi.), Wi 6:9 12:2, II Mac 10:4 A*;]
1. most freq. (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall.
2. to fall into or in (seq. εἰς, Polyb.; c. dat., II Mac 10:4).
3. to fall away (Ez 14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 22:4, Wi 6:9 12:2; in Polyb., c. gen.): absol., .
4. to fail (λόγος, Es 6:10; cf. I Ki 3:19).†

G3856.as:
† παρα-δειγματίζω (< δείκνυμι), [in LXX: Nu 25:4 (יקע hi.), Je 13:22 (חמס ni.), Ez 28:17 (רַאֲוָה), Es 4:17, Da LXX 2:5*;]
to set forth as an example; in bad sense, to put to open shame: (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

G3831.as:
πανήγυρις, -εως, ἡ (< πᾶς + ἄγυρας = ἀγορά), [in LXX: Ho 2:11 (13) 9:5, Ez 46:11 (מוֹעֵד), Am 5:21 (עֲצָרָה)*;]
prop., a national festal assembly in honour of a god; hence, generally, any festal assembly: (for exx. in π., v. MM, xviii).†
SYN.: ἐκκλησία (q.v.), συναγωγή.

G3883.as:
παρ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< παραλλάσσω), [in LXX: IV Ki 9:20 (שִׁגָּעוֹן)*;]
in various senses (LS, s.v.), change: .†

G3892.as:
παρανομία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Ps 36 (37):7 (מְזִמָּה), etc.;]
law-breaking, transgression: .†
